_note: Specific cutting force (Kienzle) per material and correction factors. Each block names its source and whether it was re-checked in that source during this project.

C45.source: kc1.1 and mc of the nearest tabulated steel E335 (St 60, Rm about 600 MPa) in the de.wikipedia table 'Spezifische Schnittkraft' (fetched 10 Nov 2026); C45 itself is not in that table, so this is an assumption of similarity. Re/Rm: EN 10083-2 C45 +N order of magnitude (from memory)

S275JR.source: same table (lower bound for the sensitivity study)

42CrMo4.source: same table (upper bound for the sensitivity study)

E355.source: cutting force: same table row as C45 (E335, the nearest tabulated grade; assumption). Re/Rm: EN 10305-1 E355 +SR as used in project 13 (data/materials.json there, not re-checked)

corrections.source: de.wikipedia 'Spezifische Schnittkraft' correction factors, citing Tschaetsch, Praxis der Zerspantechnik, 10th ed. 2011, p. 18 (fetched 10 Nov 2026). The page gives K_wear = 1.5 as a common empirical value; 1.3 is used here for a tool changed at moderate flank wear (assumption, varied 1.0-1.5).

force_ratios.source: ratio of the resultant of feed and passive force to the cutting force for coated carbide in steel; textbook order of magnitude 0.3-0.8 (from memory), varied in the sensitivity study. The split into feed and passive force follows the effective entering angle of the nose radius (Colwell equivalent cutting edge).

taylor.source: Taylor tool life vc T^n = C; n = 0.25 for coated carbide on steel is the textbook order of magnitude (from memory); C is set so that each tool's programmed vc gives 15 min (assumed design point).
